title: Dust Bowl
summary: Spanning the 1930s across the Southern Great Plains of the United States, the Dust Bowl was an environmental and agricultural disaster caused by multi-year drought and the destruction of the protective native grassland by plowing. The Oklahoma Historical Society says the dry weather began in the early 1930s and persisted through the early 1940s for some areas, with Cimarron County among the worst hit.

uncertainty.note: Severe multi-year drought spanned the 1930s, peaking in 1934–1936 and abating by 1939–1940.

as_recorded.value: early 1930s and persisted through the early 1940s

importance.justification: The Dust Bowl was one of the most severe ecological disasters in United States history, transforming federal soil conservation policy and triggering large-scale internal migration.
